Trust & protection

Clear terms, clear responsibility, clear boundaries.

These website terms are written to protect Trust&Co, define client responsibilities, allocate third-party risk clearly and establish practical rules for communication, content, payments, intellectual property and use of our services.

01 · TERMS

Terms & Conditions

By using this website, submitting an enquiry or engaging Trust&Co, the visitor or client acknowledges these terms. Services are supplied according to the scope, deliverables, timelines and commercial terms agreed for the relevant engagement. Any request outside the agreed scope may be quoted separately. Trust&Co may decline or suspend work that is unlawful, deceptive, abusive, infringing, unsafe or inconsistent with applicable law.

02 · CLIENT RESPONSIBILITIES

Client Information & Approvals

The client is responsible for providing accurate information, lawful content, required approvals, credentials where genuinely necessary, timely feedback and access needed to perform the agreed work. Delays caused by missing content, approvals, third parties, hosting, domain providers or client-side dependencies may extend delivery timelines. The client remains responsible for verifying final content before publication.

03 · CONTENT & IP

Content, Intellectual Property & Licences

The client represents that materials supplied to Trust&Co may lawfully be used for the requested purpose and do not knowingly infringe third-party rights. Client-owned content remains the client's property. Trust&Co retains ownership of its pre-existing methods, templates, reusable components, know-how, source assets and tools unless expressly assigned in a separate written agreement. Third-party assets remain subject to their licences.

04 · PAYMENT

Fees, Payment & Cancellation

Fees, milestones, taxes if applicable, deposits, payment dates, cancellation conditions and deliverables are governed by the specific commercial agreement or invoice. Work may be paused for overdue amounts. Costs already incurred for third-party services, licences, hosting, domains or other external providers may remain payable. Refunds, where any are applicable, are subject to the written commercial terms agreed for the engagement.

05 · THIRD PARTIES

Third-Party Services

Hosting companies, domain registrars, email providers, Google services, WhatsApp, social networks, analytics systems, software vendors and payment providers are independent third parties. Their availability, pricing, terms, security controls, policy changes, approvals, outages, suspensions or account decisions are outside Trust&Co's control. Trust&Co is not responsible for a third party's acts, omissions, downtime or decisions.

06 · CASHFREE

Payment Partner Disclaimer

Trust&Co may provide a referral or coordination pathway to Cashfree as a Cashfree Certified Partner. Trust&Co does not operate the payment platform, hold merchant funds, approve merchants, conduct KYC, determine transaction risk, control settlements, impose reserves or decide account restrictions. All such matters remain with Cashfree under its agreements and policies. No approval, transaction volume, settlement result or continuity of a third-party payment account is guaranteed by Trust&Co.

07 · LIABILITY

Disclaimer & Limitation of Liability

Services and website content are provided on an as-available basis and without any promise of uninterrupted operation, particular search ranking, traffic level, lead volume, sales, revenue or business outcome. To the maximum extent permitted by applicable law, Trust&Co will not be responsible for indirect, incidental, special, consequential, punitive or business-loss damages arising from third-party systems, delays, outages, data loss, cyber incidents, policy changes, client instructions or matters outside its reasonable control.

08 · INDEMNITY

Client Indemnity

To the maximum extent permitted by applicable law, the client agrees to defend, indemnify and hold harmless Trust&Co, its proprietor, personnel and service collaborators from claims, losses, liabilities, costs and reasonable expenses arising from client-supplied content, unlawful instructions, infringement claims, misuse of services, violation of third-party terms or the client's conduct in connection with the engagement.

09 · CONFIDENTIALITY

Confidential Information

Each party should use reasonable care with non-public information received from the other in connection with a project. Confidential information may be disclosed where required by law, a competent authority, professional advisers or essential service providers, or where the information was already public or independently known. Highly sensitive credentials should not be sent through ordinary website forms or email unless specifically required and securely arranged.

10 · SECURITY

Security & Data Risk

Trust&Co will use reasonable technical and organisational care appropriate to the service, but no internet transmission, hosting environment, software system or third-party platform can be guaranteed to be completely secure. The client acknowledges risks associated with phishing, malware, compromised credentials, third-party breaches, device security and internet availability. Clients should maintain secure passwords, backups and access controls.

11 · PRIVACY

Privacy Policy

Trust&Co may collect information voluntarily submitted through the website, such as name, business name, phone number, email address and enquiry details. Information may be used to respond to enquiries, prepare proposals, provide services, communicate about engagements, maintain business records, prevent abuse and meet legal obligations. Trust&Co does not intentionally request passwords, card PINs, CVV numbers, banking credentials or authentication secrets through the website enquiry form.

12 · PRIVACY CONTINUED

Data Sharing, Retention & Requests

Information may be processed by essential third-party providers used for email, hosting, communications, forms or other requested services. Trust&Co does not sell enquiry data as a business practice. Information may be retained for as long as reasonably necessary for legitimate business, contractual, accounting, security or legal purposes. Requests concerning personal information may be sent to the business contact email, subject to legal and practical limitations.

13 · ACCEPTABLE USE

Lawful Use Only

The website and services must not be used for fraud, impersonation, unlawful financial activity, malicious software, harassment, infringement, deceptive practices, unauthorised access or any activity prohibited by applicable law. Trust&Co may refuse or terminate services where it reasonably believes the requested activity presents legal, security, reputational or compliance risk.

14 · FORCE MAJEURE

Events Outside Reasonable Control

Trust&Co will not be responsible for failure or delay caused by events reasonably beyond its control, including major outages, hosting failures, internet disruptions, cyber incidents, natural events, government action, changes in law or platform policy, labour disruption, unavailable third-party services or other comparable events. Performance will resume when reasonably practicable.

15 · RELATIONSHIP

Independent Business Relationship

Unless a separate written agreement expressly states otherwise, an engagement does not create a partnership, joint venture, employment, agency, franchise or fiduciary relationship between Trust&Co and the client. A referral to a third-party provider does not make Trust&Co the provider of that third party's regulated or contractual services.

16 · GOVERNING TERMS

Governing Law & Disputes

These general website terms are intended to be interpreted under the laws applicable in India, subject to mandatory statutory rights. Parties should first attempt to resolve disputes through good-faith written communication. If a dispute cannot be resolved, jurisdiction and dispute procedures will be determined by the applicable written agreement and mandatory law, with Mumbai, Maharashtra intended as the principal business forum where legally permissible.

17 · ENTIRE AGREEMENT

Written Engagement Controls

Where a signed proposal, quotation, service agreement, statement of work, invoice or other written engagement conflicts with these general website terms, the specific written engagement will control to the extent of the conflict. No informal statement should be treated as changing agreed commercial or legal terms unless confirmed in writing by an authorised representative.

18 · SEVERABILITY

Severability & Survival

If any provision is found unenforceable or invalid under applicable law, it should be limited or removed only to the extent necessary while the remaining provisions continue to operate. Provisions concerning payment obligations, intellectual property, confidentiality, disclaimers, indemnity, limitation of liability and dispute handling are intended to continue after the relevant engagement ends to the extent permitted by law.

Important: These terms are a general business website framework and cannot guarantee protection in every possible dispute or jurisdiction. For significant contracts, regulated activities, large-value transactions or unusual risk, have the final agreement reviewed by a qualified Indian lawyer before use.
